findings.title: canManage() for Groups grants management rights with only VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2#canManage() (no-arg) calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) - exactly the same call used by canManage()'s sibling canView(). This means a caller who was only granted the VIEW scope on the all-groups ('Groups') resource (and not MANAGE) will have canManage() return true. Since GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() and other mutating endpoints call auth.groups().requireManage(), a user with view-only permission on groups can create/modify top-level groups, which is a privilege escalation. Compare with canManage(GroupModel) in the same file which correctly only checks AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE. The no-arg canManage() should only check the MANAGE scope, not VIEW+MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses Resource.getId() instead of Resource.getName() when looking up/collecting group IDs
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the lambda passed to resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) receives Resource objects whose 'name' field holds the actual Group ID (per AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup, which creates the resource with name=group.getId()). The code instead uses groupResource.getId() (the Resource entity's own internal id) both as the key passed into hasPermission(groupId, ...) - which does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) - and as the value added to the 'granted' set. Because the Resource's internal id generally does not equal the group id used as the resource name, the findByName lookup fails for every resource, hasPermission() falls back to checking only the 'all-groups' permission (which is usually absent in the per-group-permission scenario), and the returned set either stays empty or (worse) contains bogus resource IDs rather than real group IDs. This breaks group-scoped user visibility/search (UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource rely on these IDs to filter users by group membership), and should make the newly added GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest#testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers/testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers tests fail or behave incorrectly. The fix is to use groupResource.getName() instead of groupResource.getId() in both places.

findings.title: getResourceName() not extended for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to return a friendly label ('All users') for the all-users resource and the username for individual user resources, but no equivalent branch was added for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE even though this PR introduces Groups as a full resource type with the same 'all-resource vs individual resource (named by id)' pattern. As a result, scope permissions for groups will fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which for group resources is just the raw group id/UUID rather than a readable group name or an 'All groups' label, unlike the symmetric handling added for Users.

findings.title: Per-subgroup canView() re-evaluation replaces a cached global check
findings.body: getSubGroups() previously computed `boolean canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView();` once and used `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))`, so when the caller already has global view rights, no further permission evaluation was performed per subgroup. The change to `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` calls canView(GroupModel) for every subgroup, and that method internally re-invokes canView() (role check, and for V2 FGAP a full authorization policy evaluation) for every single element. For realms with many subgroups and FGAP V2 enabled, this turns one policy evaluation into N policy evaluations per request, which is a real performance regression. The same pattern was also introduced in GroupsResource.getGroups().

findings.title: Public utility method removed without deprecation
findings.body: The public static method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(KeycloakSession, RealmModel, Map<String,String>, Integer, Integer)` was removed entirely (its one-line body was simply inlined into GroupsResource). Since this is a public static method on a widely-used utility class, any external code (custom providers/extensions) calling it directly will fail to compile/link against the new version. If this method is intended to be internal-only, it should at least be deprecated before removal rather than removed outright in the same change.
